S755_primary_result_reconciliation.locator: Methods > Study design; Results > Predictive formula; Table 3; Table 4; Figure 1; Discussion > Limitations
S755_primary_result_reconciliation.confirmed: The article defines SCS success as >=50% relief during trial and subsequent implant; reports 945 included patients (826 success, 119 who failed and proceeded to TDD); and gives a logistic formula using baseline age, sex, depression, neuropathic pain, postlaminectomy syndrome and spine-related pain. Results report AUC 0.7414 and a data-derived threshold of 0.880. Discussion separately states 95% accuracy with cross-validation.
S755_primary_result_reconciliation.unresolved: The 95% accuracy claim occurs once in Discussion and has no described fold/split protocol or denominator in the article text. The Results AUC and threshold are different performance quantities and do not independently reconcile that claim. Table 3 reports postlaminectomy versus CRPS OR 1.597 (95% CI 0.935–2.727; p=0.086), whose natural log rounds to +0.468 in the Results formula; Table 4 omits this term from its five listed predictor rows. No fixed assessment horizon, model-specific complete-case N, patient-disjointness, or external validation is reported. The article does not state how row-level predictor and outcome records were joined.
S755_primary_result_reconciliation.interpretation_limit: Treat 95% as a discussion-level reported claim, not as independently reproducible or externally validated performance; do not substitute it for the reported AUC or infer patient-level leakage status.

S762_result_text_reconciliation_2026_09_.source_version: Archived copy of the LWW publisher full-text page captured 2021-09-30; live LWW route returned HTTP 403 during the current check.
S762_result_text_reconciliation_2026_09_.locators: Figure 3 caption; Results Section 3.5 / JCL-P-22; Methods Section 2.5 / JCL-P-16.
S762_result_text_reconciliation_2026_09_.confirmed: Figure 3 defines a 12-month holistic responder by all four conditions: at least 33% improvement on NRS for low-back and leg pain, at least 30% improvement on ODI, EQ-5D increase of at least 0.03, and decreased medication versus baseline; the article gives no numeric threshold for the medication decrease. Figure 3 says status is unknown when one or more 12-month outcome measures are unavailable. Results Section 3.5 instead says 5.43% could not be determined because at least one baseline measurement was missing. The article also reports 47.83% responders, 46.74% nonresponders and 5.43% indeterminate among the 92 participants still receiving HD-SCS at 12 months; the corresponding approximately 44/43/5 counts are arithmetic derivations, not printed counts.
S762_result_text_reconciliation_2026_09_.unresolved: The Figure 3 caption and Results Section 3.5 give different reasons/timepoints for indeterminate status; the source does not resolve the discrepancy. The reported 92-person 12-month denominator and derived approximately 44/43/5 categories do not establish the prediction model's fitted N. Methods Section 2.5 says only participants with complete baseline predictors entered analysis and describes an 80/20 train/validation split with five randomly created validation sets; absolute per-split N, split unit, patient-disjointness and row-level linkage are not reported. The ClinicalTrials.gov registry reports 272 actual enrollment, while the article reports 194 recruited; the checked primary sources do not reconcile these study-flow figures.
S762_result_text_reconciliation_2026_09_.interpretation_limit: Preserve the outcome-status discrepancy without inferring which missingness rule generated the five indeterminate cases. Do not report 87 as the fitted model N or infer a patient-disjoint split from the patient-level prediction task.

S034_performance_denominator_reconstruct.locators: Publisher PDF pp. 896-897, Methods > Data Management and Preprocessing and Optimized Model Development; Statistical Analysis and Results; Supplementary Table 2.
S034_performance_denominator_reconstruct.reported: N=150; separate one-year targets are NRS reduction >50% (61/150) and >70% (30/150). Publisher states an 80/20 train/test split and GridSearchCV with five stratified folds. It does not print test N, split seed, row memberships, or explicitly tie every reported metric to the held-out test set. The stratified folds are described as hyperparameter-tuning subsets, not as five independent external validations.
S034_performance_denominator_reconstruct.conditional_reconstruction: If all 150 records entered one 80/20 partition, the test partition would contain 30 records under the conventional exact 20% allocation. Reported rounded metrics are numerically consistent with 27/30 correct in each target: for >50%, sensitivity 11/13 and specificity 16/17; for >70%, sensitivity 5/6 and specificity 22/24. These are derived candidate confusion counts, not printed denominators or a source-confirmed mapping of metrics to a particular split.
S034_performance_denominator_reconstruct.interpretation_limit: Do not upgrade inferred N=30 or the reconstructed confusion counts to reported facts. The article does not identify the evaluation rows or establish that the printed metrics are computed on a single held-out partition. Imputation/scaling are described before the split; the prose order raises a leakage concern but does not establish its implementation or effect. RFE is described after GridSearchCV; whether selection was restricted within training folds is not reported. No independent external validation, reusable patient-level dataset, or ECAP predictor is reported.

indexed_primary_leads.title: Subcallosal Cingulate structural connectivity as biomarker for chronic low back pain
indexed_primary_leads.locator: Author preprint v1 source XML: Methods Sections 2.1 and 2.4; Results Sections 3.1–3.3; Table 1; Data Availability
indexed_primary_leads.confirmed: The author preprint reports baseline diffusion MRI in eight chronic-low-back-pain patients before a percutaneous SCS trial (six UCLA, two UTSW). Methods Section 2.1 defines response as >50% reduction in VAS, measured before the trial and after 15 days. Section 2.4 relates baseline SCC connectivity to binary trial response and continuous VAS change using GLM/correlation and a multiple regression with baseline HAMD. All eight are analysed as one small cohort; no train/test split or independent validation is described. This is an imaging-to-SCS-trial-response association, not an ECAP predictor or a longitudinal post-implant pain model. Data are available on reasonable request; the preprint is not peer reviewed.
indexed_primary_leads.unresolved: Patient-level MRI values and analysis code were not released for independent reuse; a public reuse licence for the underlying data was not established. No independent predictive validation or later clinical outcome is reported. The checked medRxiv/Crossref version routes do not establish a journal version. The eight-person cohort must not be merged with other SCS imaging cohorts without an explicit identity bridge.
indexed_primary_leads.next_action: Create a canonical preprint source card with the bounded 15-day trial target and no validation claim; retain PA-05 open for independently validated patient-level prediction evidence.

cohort_and_endpoint.value: The author abstract reports 939 patients in the Medtronic Product Surveillance Registry (2018-2020), enrolled after successful SCS or TDD trials before implantation; 619 SCS and 320 TDD recipients. Baseline predictors were linked to six-month outcomes. Success was at least 50% reduction of baseline VAS at six months.
cohort_and_endpoint.locator: PubMed author abstract, Materials and Methods and Results; official Elsevier Supplementary Table 2 lists SCS failed/success counts 481/138 and TDD 173/147, summing to 619 and 320.

validation_metrics.supplement_table_1: SCS sensitivity 67% (58-74), specificity 93% (91-95), PPV 74% (66-80), NPV 91% (88-93), accuracy 87% (84-90); TDD sensitivity 88% (82-93), specificity 67% (59-74), PPV 69% (64-74), NPV 87% (81-92), accuracy 77% (72-81); subgroup summaries are also reported.
validation_metrics.supplement_table_2: Per-class precision/recall/F1 and counts: SCS failed 481, succeeded 138; TDD failed 173, succeeded 147.
validation_metrics.supplement_figure_3: Text reports combined, SCS and TDD accuracy 83.7%, 87.3% and 76.8%, and AUC 82%, 80% and 78%, respectively. These are classification accuracy and discrimination measures, not interchangeable.

external_validation_and_limits.confirmed: The abstract describes a prospective multicenter registry validation of a formula developed retrospectively at one center and calls the registry data an independent external validation. This is clinically relevant validation evidence for the original S755 formula.
not_reported_or_unresolved: The PubMed abstract defines responders as >=50% VAS reduction, while the official supplement defines an event as >50%; the exact handling of equality at 50% cannot be resolved without the full analysis code or participant rows.
No train/test split, fold assignment, calibration, AUC confidence interval, model refitting procedure, or participant-level split membership is reported in the abstract or supplement.
Supplementary Figure 2 is an image; exact TP/FP/TN/FN cells were not machine-readable from the DOCX text, though class counts and aggregate metrics are reported.
No individual patient rows or analysis code are in the supplement. Data-availability statement and additional body-text details remain unverified because publisher article body returned HTTP 403.

Registry-site multicenter description is reported, but participant-level overlap cannot be independently tested without row-level data. No ECAP predictor is reported in the accessible abstract or supplement.
